en: Mayon Volcano in Albay features a nearly perfect symmetrical cone shape that is easily observable from miles away.
The Puerto Princesa Subterranean River in Palawan features a navigable underground river that flows directly into the sea.
Taal Lake in Batangas occupies a large volcanic caldera where observers can see steep inner cliff walls.
Mount Apo in Davao features observable geothermal activity, including naturally heated hot springs visible along its hiking trails.
The Tubbataha Reefs in the Sulu Sea feature visible coral atolls with vibrant marine life observable just below the surface.
The amihan wind brings cool, dry northeast monsoon air that observers feel across the Philippines between December and February.
Trees in the mossy forests of Mount Kitanglad in Bukidnon are visibly covered in thick, moisture-retaining epiphytic plants.
The Chocolate Hills in Bohol consist of over 1,200 symmetrical limestone mounds that turn brown during the dry season.
The Hinatuan Enchanted River in Surigao del Sur exhibits remarkably clear, deep blue water originating from underground springs.
Mount Pinatubo's massive caldera, formed by a 1991 eruption, now holds a highly visible, deep crater lake.
Strong, visible ocean currents in the Verde Island Passage between Batangas and Mindoro support highly diverse coral reefs.
Great Santa Cruz Island in Zamboanga features pink sand created by crushed red organ pipe coral fragments.
